name: http_request
description:
Make an HTTP request to any REST/JSON API. Use this for any service that exposes an HTTP API — Bluesky (AT Protocol: createSession, createRecord, getTimeline, etc.), Mastodon, Reddit, GitHub, Spotify, WHOOP, OpenAI, Anthropic, Polymarket, OnStar, any social / productivity / finance / health platform. Also covers generic REST endpoints, webhooks, OAuth token endpoints, and JSON POSTs. Headers and body may carry `datapod:` references — sealed pod values (auth tokens, API keys, app passwords, sensitive payloads) the tool resolves at courier scope; the resolved values never enter your transcript. Per-field pod substitution inside dict bodies IS supported (recurses into nested dicts and lists). Optionally seal the response into a new pod with a declared privacy class so the response body is also kept out of your transcript.

Use for REST APIs (public or authenticated). For browser-rendered pages or stateful sessions, use playwright_manager instead.

Pod-reference format in header values OR inside body fields: `datapod:<kind>:<id>` (implicit 'full' projection) or `datapod:<kind>:<id>/<projection>` (explicit).

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: Target URL. Plain string; the URL itself is not pod-resolvable.

inputs.name: method
inputs.description: HTTP method. One of GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD. Default GET.

inputs.name: headers
inputs.description: Request headers as a {name: value} dict. Any value starting with `datapod:` is resolved at courier scope; the resolved string never appears in your transcript. Use for Authorization, X-API-Key, etc.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: Request body, ALWAYS a string. For JSON APIs, pass a JSON-encoded string — the tool json.loads it at execute time and sends it as JSON. Per-field pod substitution IS supported inside that JSON: any string field whose value starts with `datapod:` resolves at courier scope (recurses into nested dicts and lists). For a sealed payload, pass a single `datapod:<kind>:<id>/<projection>` reference — the whole body comes from the pod. For raw text bodies, pass the literal string. Example for Bluesky createSession: `"{\"identifier\": \"<handle>\", \"password\": \"datapod:auth.bearer:<id>/full\"}"`.

inputs.name: query_params
inputs.description: URL query params as a {name: value} dict. Appended to the URL.

inputs.name: response_pod_kind
inputs.description: If set, seal the response body into a new pod with this privacy class (e.g. 'health.private', 'financial.private'). The tool returns the new pod_id instead of the body; the response content never enters your transcript. Use for sensitive data you should not read.

inputs.name: seal_fields
inputs.description: List of top-level field names in the response JSON to seal into pods. Each named field is replaced in the response body with a `datapod:<seal_pod_kind>:<id>/full` reference; the real value goes into a fresh pod. Subsequent http_request calls can reference that pod-ref verbatim in a header value (e.g. `Authorization: Bearer datapod:auth.session:<id>/full`) and the tool resolves it at courier scope. Use whenever a service returns a credential the next call needs to relay — e.g. Bluesky's createSession returns `accessJwt`/`refreshJwt`; pass `seal_fields: ["accessJwt", "refreshJwt"]` and the JWT never enters your transcript (LLM transcription corrupts long opaque strings, see project_http_request_inbound_credential_sealing).

inputs.name: seal_pod_kind
inputs.description: Pod kind to use when sealing fields via `seal_fields`. Defaults to 'auth.session'. The authority class is derived from the kind suffix (.private/.gated/.chat/.public) or falls through to AUTH_USER for unknown suffixes — 'auth.session' falls through, matching 'auth.bearer'.

inputs.name: follow_redirects
inputs.description: Whether to follow HTTP redirects. Default true.

inputs.name: expect_status
inputs.description: If set, the call fails if the response status is not in this list. E.g. [200, 201] to fail on any error response.

outputs.description: Human-readable status: method, host, status code, response bytes, response pod_id if sealed.
Structured payload: status, headers (response), content_type, content_length, body (if not sealed), response_pod_id (if sealed), duration_ms.

arguments_prompt:
Arguments for http_request:
url: str                           # target URL
method: str = 'GET'                # GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/HEAD
headers: Optional[dict]            # values may be `datapod:` refs (sealed auth)
body: Optional[str]                # JSON-encoded string for JSON APIs (parsed at execute), raw text, or `datapod:` ref
query_params: Optional[dict]
timeout_s: float = 30.0
response_pod_kind: Optional[str]   # if set, seal response in pod with this class
seal_fields: Optional[list[str]]   # top-level fields to seal into pods (e.g. ['accessJwt','refreshJwt']) — replaced in response body with pod-refs the next call can relay verbatim. LLM never sees the bytes.
seal_pod_kind: Optional[str]       # pod kind for seal_fields. Default 'auth.session'.
follow_redirects: bool = True
expect_status: Optional[list[int]] # fail if status not in list

metadata.planner_description: Generic HTTP/REST tool — your default for ANY JSON API: Bluesky/AT Protocol, Mastodon, Reddit, GitHub, Spotify, WHOOP, OAuth token exchanges, webhooks. Pod-aware auth (header values) AND per-field pod-aware body (e.g. `{"password": "datapod:auth.bearer:.../full"}`). Optional pod-sealed responses for sensitive data. Use playwright_manager only for browser-rendered or stateful sessions.
